title: Claudia Sheinbaum Projects Economic Rebound in Mexico for the Second Half of the Year
author: Néstor Jiménez
content:
_This article by Néstor Jiménez and Alonso Urrutia originally appeared in
the[July 6, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/07/06/economia/claudia-
sheinbaum-proyecta-repunte-economico-en-mexico-para-el-segundo-semestre-del-
ano), Mexico's premier left-wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City.** During the second half of this year, an upturn in the
country's economic indicators is projected, President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo
affirmed. "We are going to do better in the second half; there are already
some second-quarter indicators, and from now on, July toward December, there
will be better indicators."

She maintained that the housing-for-wellbeing program is helping to "move"
those indicators, even though it "has not yet reached its peak of job
creation."

During her Monday press conference, she explained that the auto-parts and
manufacturing sectors are growing significantly, mainly the manufacture of
electronics.

Referring to the country's record automobile sales according to figures from
the National Institute of Statistics and Geography (Inegi), the president said
this "speaks to the purchasing capacity that exists; consumption is boosted,"
and she linked it to the goals set out within Plan México to produce more for
the domestic market.

Meanwhile, she recalled that on July 20 a team from the U.S. government will
come to the country to continue the conversations on the review of the Treaty
on Trade between Mexico, the United States, and Canada.

"We continue in dialogue with the U.S. government with the idea that it not
create uncertainty, but rather that investment be guaranteed for this and
coming years," she added.
